roles.title: Assistant Game Designer
roles.description: Shape player experiences through ideas, systems and iteration.
roles.flavor: Mechanics are your medium. Systems are your story.

roles.title: Broadcast Production Assistant
roles.description: Help run the live stream: camera, graphics, audio and show flow.
roles.flavor: The show only looks effortless because someone made it so.

roles.title: Esports Coach
roles.description: Guide a squad's strategy, practice plans and in-game decision making.
roles.flavor: A great coach turns raw talent into a team.

roles.title: Esports Community Manager
roles.description: Keep a game or team's community active, welcoming and well moderated.
roles.flavor: A healthy community is the best marketing there is.

roles.title: Esports Data Analyst
roles.description: Turn match and audience data into insight for teams and organisers.
roles.flavor: Numbers don't lie, but they do need translating.

roles.title: Esports Development Officer
roles.description: Grow grassroots participation and pathways into competitive gaming.
roles.flavor: Someone has to build the ladder before others can climb it.

roles.title: Esports Event Assistant
roles.description: Help tournaments, leagues and live gaming events run smoothly.
roles.flavor: From LAN parties to arena shows — you make the magic happen behind the scenes.

roles.title: Esports Journalist / Photographer
roles.description: Cover matches, players and stories for fans following the scene.
roles.flavor: Someone has to be there to tell people what happened.

roles.title: Esports Marketing & Partnerships Assistant
roles.description: Support sponsorships, campaigns, brand activity and fan engagement.
roles.flavor: Stories and sponsorships connect fans to the game. You craft the bridge between brands and communities.

roles.title: Esports Performance Analyst
roles.description: Study match data and VODs to find patterns that improve a team's play.
roles.flavor: The story is always in the data.

roles.title: Esports Performance Coach
roles.description: Support players' mindset, routines and consistency under competitive pressure.
roles.flavor: Peak performance starts long before the match.

roles.title: Esports Venue Operations Assistant
roles.description: Help gaming venues, arenas and facilities run safely and smoothly.
roles.flavor: A great event runs on invisible work. You make sure the stage, the seats, and the schedule all line up.

roles.title: Gaming Community Assistant
roles.description: Help players connect through thoughtful, welcoming communities.
roles.flavor: The best games are the ones people play together. You build the spaces where that happens.

roles.title: Junior Game Artist
roles.description: Create characters, props and environments that bring a game to life.
roles.flavor: Every asset on screen started as someone's sketch.

roles.title: Junior Game Producer
roles.description: Keep a development team on track: schedules, communication and priorities.
roles.flavor: Someone has to hold the whole picture in view.

roles.title: Junior QA Tester
roles.description: Find bugs and help make sure a game works the way it should.
roles.flavor: Every shipped game was once full of bugs someone found first.

roles.title: Player Wellbeing & Recovery Assistant
roles.description: Help players build sustainable routines and find appropriate support.
roles.flavor: The game never stops, but players need to. You keep talent healthy, focused, and ready to perform.

roles.title: Team Operations Coordinator
roles.description: Coordinate schedules, travel and logistics behind a competitive team.
roles.flavor: Great teams run on great logistics.

cards.name: Attend Esports Expo
cards.description: Visit an esports expo and network with industry professionals.
cards.flavor: Networking is key.

cards.name: Attend Employer Visit
cards.description: Ask prepared questions, observe workflows and note one thing you learned.
cards.flavor: You're not a tourist. You're scouting your future.

cards.name: Check Player Wellbeing
cards.description: Check in on rest, workload and mood before a big event.
cards.flavor: Burnt-out players don't perform.

cards.name: Coordinate Partner Stream
cards.description: Coordinate a co-stream event with a partner content creator.
cards.flavor: Collaboration amplifies reach.

cards.name: Create Promo Content
cards.description: Create social media and promotional content for an event or product.
cards.flavor: Content drives engagement.

cards.name: Create Tournament Promo
cards.description: Spend focused time producing a poster, short video, social post, or stream overlay.
cards.flavor: Making the thing is always the hardest part.

cards.name: Judge Community Tournament
cards.description: Judge matches in a community tournament and provide feedback.
cards.flavor: Every judge shapes the future.

cards.name: Manage Player Roster
cards.description: Handle player contracts, substitutions, and team composition.
cards.flavor: The business of esports.

cards.name: Negotiate Sponsorship Deal
cards.description: Negotiate a sponsorship deal with a brand partner.
cards.flavor: Words matter.

cards.name: Operate the Live Stream
cards.description: Run camera, graphics or audio during a live broadcast.
cards.flavor: The stream is the show — and the show must go on.

cards.name: Plan a Practice Session
cards.description: Design a practice block with clear goals for a squad or player.
cards.flavor: A plan turns practice into progress.

cards.name: Publish Event Coverage
cards.description: Write up or photograph an event for publication.
cards.flavor: If it isn't published, it didn't happen — as far as the internet's concerned.

cards.name: Review Match VODs
cards.description: Watch back recent matches and note patterns worth acting on.
cards.flavor: The replay never lies.

cards.name: Run a Community Session
cards.description: Host a Q&A, watch party or community event for fans or players.
cards.flavor: Communities grow around people who show up.

cards.name: Run Training Session
cards.description: Run a training session for aspiring players.
cards.flavor: Coach the next generation.

cards.name: Set Up Match Day
cards.description: Prepare kit, seating, signage and schedules ahead of a live event.
cards.flavor: Match day starts hours before the first game.

cards.name: Track Player Metrics
cards.description: Log stats across sessions to spot trends in performance.
cards.flavor: If you can't measure it, you're guessing.

cards.description: Choose a role — registration, player support, setup, social posts, or match scheduling — and get stuck in.
cards.flavor: Tournaments run on volunteers like you.

cards.name: Research Industry Standards
cards.description: Study current best practices, pipelines, and quality bars for your discipline.
cards.flavor: Know the bar before you raise it.

cards.name: Create Personal Learning Plan
cards.description: Map skills to acquire, resources to use, and milestones to hit during the experience.
cards.flavor: A plan turns hope into progress.

cards.name: Set Up Portfolio Tracking
cards.description: Create a system to capture work-in-progress, feedback, and final pieces for your portfolio.
cards.flavor: Document as you go, not after.

cards.name: Establish Communication Routines
cards.description: Agree on check-in frequency, update formats, and escalation paths with your supervisor.
cards.flavor: Communication is a skill, not an afterthought.

cards.name: Define Success Metrics
cards.description: Agree on what "done well" looks like: quality, speed, innovation, or player impact.
cards.flavor: You can't hit a target you can't see.

cards.name: Prepare Questions for Mentor
cards.description: List specific technical, creative, and career questions to maximize mentor sessions.
cards.flavor: Good questions get better answers.

cards.name: Prototype a Core System
cards.description: Build a quick proof-of-concept for a key mechanic, tool, or pipeline.
cards.flavor: Prototypes answer questions designs can't.

cards.name: Collaborate Cross-Discipline
cards.description: Work with a different discipline (art/code/design) to integrate a feature end-to-end.
cards.flavor: Great games are built at discipline boundaries.

cards.name: Optimize a Workflow
cards.description: Identify a bottleneck and implement a faster process, script, or template.
cards.flavor: Automation compounds.

cards.name: Run a Playtest Session
cards.description: Observe players, take notes, and identify friction points in the experience.
cards.flavor: Players reveal what designers miss.

cards.name: Create Technical Documentation
cards.description: Write clear docs for a system, API, or pipeline so others can use and maintain it.
cards.flavor: Documentation is empathy for your future self.

cards.name: Refactor for Maintainability
cards.description: Clean up messy code, rigs, or files to improve readability and reduce future bugs.
cards.flavor: Clean craft enables speed.

cards.name: Record Peer Feedback
cards.description: Document specific feedback from teammates and how you acted on it.
cards.flavor: Feedback implemented is growth demonstrated.

cards.name: Capture Before/After Comparison
cards.description: Show side-by-side evidence of improvement: performance, quality, or player experience.
cards.flavor: Visual proof needs no translation.

cards.name: Write a Case Study Outline
cards.description: Structure a portfolio case study: problem, process, solution, result, reflection.
cards.flavor: Case studies get you hired.

cards.name: Collect Quantitative Metrics
cards.description: Gather data: frame rates, load times, player retention, iteration speed, bug counts.
cards.flavor: Numbers convince skeptics.

cards.name: Document a Failure & Recovery
cards.description: Record what went wrong, root cause analysis, and the fix that prevented recurrence.
cards.flavor: Failures documented become wisdom.

cards.name: Create a Showcase Video/GIF
cards.description: Record a 30-second clip of your work in context: in-engine, in-game, or in-pipeline.
cards.flavor: Show, don't just tell.

cards.name: Feature Adopted by Team
cards.description: Your prototype, tool, or process was adopted as standard practice by the team.
cards.flavor: Adoption is the ultimate validation.

cards.name: Mentored a Peer
cards.description: Helped another student/junior improve their skills through guidance and knowledge sharing.
cards.flavor: Teaching proves mastery.

cards.name: Contributed to Shipped Content
cards.description: Your work is part of content that reached players, even in a small way.
cards.flavor: Shipped is the only metric that counts.

cards.name: Wild Card: Industry Veteran Insight
cards.description: A veteran shares hard-won wisdom. Use in place of any Setup, Action, or Proof card for any set.
cards.flavor: Experience is the best teacher.

cards.name: Wild Card: Cross-Discipline Workshop
cards.description: An intensive workshop bridges disciplines. Use in place of any card for any set.
cards.flavor: Boundaries are where innovation lives.

cards.name: Wild Card: Personal Project Sprint
cards.description: A focused personal project fills a gap. Use in place of any card for any set.
cards.flavor: Self-directed work shows drive.

cards.name: Build a Sponsor Activation
cards.description: Design a small on-site or online activity for a sponsor's brand.
cards.flavor: Sponsors fund the scene — treat them well.

cards.name: Coordinate Volunteer Roles
cards.description: Assign shifts, brief volunteers on their roles, and set up a communication channel for the day.
cards.flavor: Herd management, esports edition.

cards.name: Complete Partner Task
cards.description: Complete the agreed task and ask the partner for feedback.
cards.flavor: Professional feedback is worth more than a grade.

cards.name: Complete Partner Project
cards.description: Work with an industry partner, act on feedback and deliver agreed outcomes.
cards.flavor: Professional feedback is the fastest way to level up.

cards.name: Complete Placement Tasks
cards.description: Choose a focus — event operations, streaming support, social media, player support, or equipment setup — and do the work.
cards.flavor: This is where the CV entry actually gets written.

cards.name: Deliver the Live Brief
cards.description: Finish and present work to the brief. Respond to feedback and iterate.
cards.flavor: Done is better than perfect. Shipped is better than done.

cards.name: Finish Skills Assignment
cards.description: Complete a course assignment that demonstrates subject knowledge relevant to your role.
cards.flavor: Grades open doors. Skills keep them open.

cards.name: Revise After Feedback
cards.description: Improve work using specific feedback. Shows growth mindset and resilience.
cards.flavor: First draft is for you. Second draft is for them.

cards.name: Run a Coaching Session
cards.description: Deliver a one-to-one or small-group coaching moment focused on a specific skill.
cards.flavor: The best coaches listen more than they speak.

cards.name: Measure Your Contribution
cards.description: Explain what changed because of your work, using a result, feedback or clear example.
cards.flavor: Show the difference your contribution made.

cards.name: Share Partner Feedback
cards.description: Record the partner's response to your completed work and how it met their objectives.
cards.flavor: External validation is the gold standard of achievement.

cards.name: Share Partner Outcome
cards.description: Present the finished result to the partner and explain how you used their feedback.
cards.flavor: A strong partnership leaves both sides with something useful.

cards.name: Show Placement Impact
cards.description: Summarise the result of your placement work and how it helped the esports team or event.
cards.flavor: Show what changed because you were there.

cards.name: Showcase Placement Result
cards.description: Present the final outcome of your placement work — a demo, report, or deliverable — and explain its impact.
cards.flavor: The best placements end with a story worth telling.

cards.name: Ask for a Reference
cards.description: Request written feedback from someone who supervised your work.
cards.flavor: A reference is a vote of confidence in writing.

cards.name: Write a CV Achievement
cards.description: Describe your contribution, the skill you used and the measurable outcome.
cards.flavor: Don't list duties. List impact.

cards.name: Daily Log & Reflection
cards.description: Record what you did, what you learned and how it connects to your target role.
cards.flavor: Experience unrecorded is experience forgotten.

cards.name: Debug & Learning Log
cards.description: Document a bug or unexpected issue you hit, the steps you took to diagnose it, and what you learned.
cards.flavor: Every bug is a lesson in disguise.

cards.name: Distinction Earned
cards.description: Bonus evidence: subject excellence.
cards.flavor: Excellence isn't an accident. It's the result of intention.

cards.name: Document Brief Learnings
cards.description: Write up what the brief taught you about your role, the client's needs, and your design decisions.
cards.flavor: A written record is the bridge between doing and reflecting.

cards.name: Reflect on Coaching Feedback
cards.description: Document how coaching conversations helped a player improve their performance or mindset.
cards.flavor: Coaching lives in the follow-through.

cards.name: Log Placement Hours & Reflection
cards.description: Record your hours and write what you did, what you learned, and how it connects to your target job.
cards.flavor: Evidence is what turns a placement into a reference.

cards.name: Placement Reflection
cards.description: Write a mid-point or final reflection on your placement tasks, challenges overcome, and skills developed.
cards.flavor: Reflection turns experience into evidence.

cards.name: Present & Reflect on Feedback
cards.description: Present your work, note the feedback, and save the final version for your portfolio.
cards.flavor: Feedback is free improvement if you actually listen.

cards.name: Record Industry Insight
cards.description: Write up one thing you learned and how it changes your view of the job.
cards.flavor: Insight only counts once it's written down.

cards.name: Reliability Check-In
cards.description: Explain how you'll confirm your shift and contact the organiser if plans change.
cards.flavor: Reliability is a skill, not a personality trait.

cards.name: Revise With Feedback
cards.description: Use the partner's feedback to improve your work before it goes in your portfolio.
cards.flavor: The revision is where the real learning happens.

cards.name: Save Portfolio Evidence
cards.description: Keep a finished work sample and explain your role, tools used and outcome.
cards.flavor: Your portfolio is your proof. Make it undeniable.

cards.name: Showcase Partner Work
cards.description: Document the deliverables produced during the partnership, highlighting your specific contribution and the skills applied.
cards.flavor: The best partnerships leave a paper trail of success.

cards.name: Volunteer Feedback
cards.description: Collect and record feedback from the event organiser or fellow volunteers about your contribution.
cards.flavor: A thank-you note is worth more than a certificate.

cards.name: Agree Dates & Times
cards.description: Confirm the schedule and hours in writing. Must fit college hours (8:30am–5:30pm, max 8hr day).
cards.flavor: Verbal agreements evaporate. Written ones stick.

cards.name: Agree Your Role
cards.description: Clarify tasks, responsibilities, supervision and what you'll produce.
cards.flavor: Undefined work is unpaid work. Define it.

cards.name: Confirm Partner Project
cards.description: Find out who the industry partner is, what the project involves, when sessions happen, and what they expect you to produce.
cards.flavor: Partnerships work best with clear expectations on both sides.

cards.name: Confirm Venue Logistics
cards.description: Book the venue, confirm access, arrange equipment, and create a run sheet for the event.
cards.flavor: The devil is in the details, and the angels love a well-run event.

cards.name: Employer Contact
cards.description: Get a named contact and a way to reach them — email, phone, LinkedIn.
cards.flavor: A name on a spreadsheet becomes a mentor in real life.

cards.name: Find an Organisation
cards.description: Identify a studio, team, publisher or community that matches your career goal.
cards.flavor: Every journey starts with a destination in mind.

cards.name: Partner Expectations
cards.description: Find out what the industry partner expects you to produce and how they'll support you.
cards.flavor: Partners don't want free labour. They want fresh perspective.

cards.name: Review the Brief
cards.description: Read the brief, identify the audience, check the deadline, and decide what you'll make.
cards.flavor: A clear brief saves three drafts later.

cards.name: Stage the Run Sheet
cards.description: Create a detailed run sheet with roles, timings, contacts and contingency plans for the event.
cards.flavor: A good run sheet saves the day before anyone knows there was a problem.

cards.name: Travel & Access Plan
cards.description: Check location, travel, equipment needs and any access requirements.
cards.flavor: The best plan fails if you can't get through the door.

cards.name: Understand the Brief
cards.description: Clarify the audience, deliverable, deadline and success criteria with the client.
cards.flavor: A brief misunderstood is a project doomed.

cards.name: Wild Card: Evidence Boost
cards.description: A second pair of eyes strengthens your evidence. Use this card in place of a Proof card for a Block Placement.
cards.flavor: Evidence worth keeping is evidence worth boosting.

cards.name: Wild Card: Extra Time
cards.description: A brief extension to get the work right. Use this card in place of an Action card for a Live Project Brief.
cards.flavor: Time is the one resource you can never get back.

cards.name: Wild Card: Tutor Advice
cards.description: A quick check-in with your tutor. Use this card in place of a Setup card for Volunteering.
cards.flavor: Sometimes the right words at the right time change everything.

cards.name: Wild Card: Careers Team
cards.description: The Careers & Employability team steps in. Use this card in place of any Setup, Action or Proof card for a Block Placement.
cards.flavor: They've seen every version of this problem before.

cards.name: Wild Card: Mentor Advice
cards.description: A mentor points you in the right direction. Use this card in place of any Setup, Action or Proof card for a Live Project Brief.
cards.flavor: Sometimes the fastest route is someone who's done it before.

sets.name: Block Placement
sets.why: A placement gives practical experience and, if it goes well, an employer reference.

sets.name: Employer Visit
sets.why: A visit builds industry understanding and useful contacts.

sets.name: Volunteering
sets.why: Volunteering shows reliability, initiative and teamwork.

sets.name: Live Project Brief
sets.why: A finished brief creates a portfolio piece that shows you can respond to a client's needs.

sets.name: Industry Partnership
sets.why: A partnership gives you specialist feedback and experience working with professionals.
